abstract_research_topics.justification: Density estimation is a theoretical topic that involves estimating the probability distribution for a dataset. It is foundational in understanding complex data patterns in deep learning.
Gaussian process regression is an abstract research topic in machine learning focused on probabilistic models and uncertainty quantification, often used in deep learning.
G-equivariant networks deal with mathematical properties of symmetry and equivariance, making them a more theoretical topic in deep learning research.
3D rotational equivariance involves abstract concepts of how networks can handle rotations in 3D space mathematically, a theoretical exploration.
Equivariance in neural networks explores theoretical aspects of designing architectures that maintain certain symmetries, which is inherently abstract.
Equivariant deep learning is concerned with maintaining certain properties under transformations, reflecting a theoretical aspect of network architecture design.
3D equivariance examines theoretical issues of how systems handle spatial transformations, indicating an abstract area of research.
Reproducing kernel Hilbert space is a mathematical framework used in theoretical machine learning, relevant to deep learning kernel methods.
Linear quadratic Gaussian systems are related to control theory, focusing on theoretical aspects of optimization and estimation in dynamic systems.

application_domains.justification: Memory research is applied in developing models that can retain and retrieve information, useful in real-world applications like chatbots and recommendation systems.
Auxiliary tasks are applied techniques used to enhance model learning in practical scenarios, such as multitask learning frameworks.
Catastrophic forgetting addresses a practical problem in deep learning where models forget previously learned information when learning new tasks.
Memory-augmented neural networks are applied architectures designed to improve learning and recall capacity, useful in applications like question answering.
Long-term memory in neural networks is an applied domain focusing on models' ability to retain information over extended periods, critical in various AI applications.
Game playing is an application domain where deep reinforcement learning techniques are used to develop intelligent systems capable of playing games.
Working memory refers to the application domain where models handle multiple pieces of information simultaneously, similar to human cognitive processes.
Density functional theory simulations are an application domain where deep learning models aid in simulating quantum mechanical systems.
Game theory applications use deep learning models to simulate and analyze competitive environments, such as economics and strategic decision-making.
Though having theoretical underpinnings, equivariant neural networks are increasingly applied in real-world applications, such as molecular modeling, due to their ability to handle symmetry in data.
Experience replay is an applied technique used in reinforcement learning to efficiently use past interactions to improve future decisions.
Forgetting in deep learning refers to applied techniques to mitigate the issue of models losing previously learned information.
Intrinsic rewards optimization is an application domain focusing on enhancing learning by optimizing internal evaluation criteria for artificial agents.
Auxiliary objectives are applied in practical deep learning models to improve the primary task through additional related tasks.
Intrinsic motivation in AI systems is an application domain where models derive self-motivation to improve their learning process and adaptivity.
Optimization of intrinsic rewards is focused on practical implementations in reinforcement learning to motivate agents through internal rather than external rewards.
